wv_cheat_canyon.blurb: Cheat Canyon cuts through northern West Virginia along the Cheat River, and most of its climbing sits on the canyon's north-facing side. It is overwhelmingly a bouldering destination, with only a sprinkling of sport, trad and top-rope lines, mostly between 5.7 and 5.13. Problems start at the easiest grades, bulge through the V1 to V5 middle, and stretch into double digits. The stone is sandstone that shifts from soft and pocketed to cobbly to fine and crimpy, so styles mix. In the wildlife management area the boulders favour slopers, catch plenty of sun and dry fast, which suits summer. Darnell Hollow, Snake Hill and the University Research Forest hold the biggest clusters.

me_a_western_mountains.blurb: Western Maine's mountains lie north of Lake Sebago and stretch west of the Bigelow Range, sharing much of their feel with New Hampshire's White Mountains. Trad and sport are close to evenly matched, with a good number of boulders and a winter ice scene at places such as Grafton Notch. Roped routes mostly fall between 5.9 and 5.12, thickest at 5.10 and 5.11, while the boulders lean easy to moderate. Rock changes by crag: Tumble Down Dick has metamorphic schist on a sunny face with many routes at 5.10 and under, and Bald Bluff mixes a basalt dike with schist walls. Crags are scattered, a car is essential, and plants quickly reclaim the rock. Ten Degree Wall and Chain of Ponds are mainly trad.

ca_box_springs_mountain_reserve.blurb: Box Springs Mountain Reserve is a rugged, roughly 3,400-acre stretch of steep hills between Riverside and Moreno Valley, in the Inland Empire. Bouldering makes up almost all of the climbing, with a modest number of short single-pitch trad, sport and top-rope routes between about 5.3 and 5.12. Problems run from the easiest grades up to around V6, with plenty at the lowest end. The rock is solid granite with cracks and faces. Most areas need a stiff hike uphill, though Pigeon Pass is gentler and more level. Late fall through early spring is the comfortable window; summers are hot with little shade. Belvedere Heights, Sugarloaf Mountain and Hidden Springs hold most of the boulders.

ca_buttermilk_country.blurb: Buttermilk Country sits near Bishop, on the western edge of the Owens Valley in the eastern foothills of the Sierra Nevada. The setting is high desert with meadows, small streams and rocky hills, scattered with large boulders of quartz monzonite that glaciers once carried in from elsewhere. Bouldering is the main event, famous for tall highball problems; grades run from V0 into the highest numbers, with the bulk in the V0 to V9 range. A modest number of trad routes, mostly around 5.10, share the area. Spring and fall are considered ideal, summer days are hot, and winter suits hard problems best. Buttermilks Main is the largest sub-area, followed by Buttermilk Crags and Dale's Camp.

ok_tulsa_area.blurb: Tulsa's climbing is mostly bouldering near the city, with a smaller number of sport and top-rope routes and very little trad. Most of the rock is short, around bouldering height, with just a few places offering roped climbing. The region holds both limestone and sandstone: Chandler Park, along the Arkansas River on the west side of Tulsa, is limestone and generally good quality, while sandstone in northeast Oklahoma is soft and needs several days to dry after rain. Problems run from the easiest grades to the V10 range, concentrated between V1 and V6, and roped routes mostly span 5.6 to 5.13. Chandler Park, Zen Pen, Avery Drive and Shotgun are the biggest sub-areas.

nc_rumbling_bald.blurb: Rumbling Bald lies in Hickory Nut Gorge just outside Chimney Rock, in western North Carolina. The rock is granite and gneiss, with crack and friction climbing on slabs and overhanging roof cracks. Bouldering and trad are the two main draws, with a smaller sport selection; roped routes mostly fall between 5.9 and 5.12, thickest at 5.10 and 5.11, and boulder problems run from V0 to the V11 range. Its south-facing exposure makes it a staple of the winter circuit across the region, and it is best in the cooler months. The bouldering zone is the largest sub-area, while Cereal Buttress, Hanging Chain and Comatose Area hold much of the roped climbing.
